name: The Presentation of the Lord
history: Forty days after His birth, Mary and Joseph brought Jesus to the Temple in Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord, as the Law of Moses required. There the old man Simeon took Him in his arms and greeted Him as the light of the nations, and the prophetess Anna spoke of Him to all who were waiting. Candles are blessed today, and the feast is called Candlemas.
life: The Law required that a firstborn son be offered to God and redeemed, and that a mother be purified after childbirth. Mary and Joseph, too poor to offer a lamb, brought a pair of turtle doves or two young pigeons. Saint Luke tells that Simeon, a just and devout man, had been promised that he would not die before seeing the Christ. Taking the child, he blessed God in the words of the Nunc Dimittis, sung each night at Compline, and warned Mary that a sword would pierce her own soul. The feast was kept in Jerusalem by the fourth century and in Rome by the seventh. The blessing of candles and the procession recall Christ the light entering His temple. In England, Candlemas was long one of the great days of the year. Since 1997 it has also been the World Day for Consecrated Life, for all who, like the child Jesus, are offered to God.
prayerTo: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you were carried into your Temple in your mother’s arms and received by the faithful who had waited for you. Let me wait for you as Simeon did, welcome you as Anna did, and offer myself to the Father with you. Let me depart in peace when my eyes have seen your salvation. Amen.
penance: Bring a candle to be blessed, or light one at home tonight and pray the Nunc Dimittis. Pray for monks, nuns and religious who have offered their lives to God.
meditation: Simeon waited his whole life and was not disappointed. What are you waiting for from God, and will you go on waiting in hope?
prayer: Almighty, eternal God, we humbly beseech Your majesty that, as Your only-begotten Son was this day presented in the temple in the nature of our flesh, so may You grant us to be presented to You with purified minds. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
